questions.q: With reference to the establishment of the Minorities Commission in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was initially set up in 1978 through an executive resolution of the Government of India. 2️⃣ The commission was established to safeguard the interests of minorities despite constitutional safeguards. 3️⃣ The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was constituted in the same year the Act was passed in 1992.
questions.e: The Minorities Commission was set up via executive resolution in 1978. While the National Commission for Minorities Act was passed in 1992, the first statutory Commission was actually constituted in 1993. The resolution stated that despite constitutional safeguards, a feeling of inequality persisted among minorities.

questions.q: Which of the following religious communities were notified as 'minorities' by the Central Government in 1993? 1️⃣ Muslims and Christians 2️⃣ Sikhs and Buddhists 3️⃣ Zoroastrians (Parsis) 4️⃣ Jains
questions.e: In 1993, the Centre notified five religious communities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, and Zoroastrians (Parsis). The Jain community was only added to this list much later, in 2014.

questions.q: Regarding the composition of the National Commission for Minorities, which statement is correct?
o: At least five members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities
The Vice-Chairperson is not counted as a member of the Commission
It consists of a Chairperson and six members
All members must be from minority communities
questions.e: The Commission is a multi-member body consisting of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and five members. Notably, the Act stipulates that five members, including the Chairperson, should be from among the minority communities.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the tenure and removal of members of the National Commission for Minorities: 1️⃣ The Chairperson and members hold office for a term of five years. 2️⃣ A member can be removed if they absent themselves from three consecutive meetings without leave. 3️⃣ The Central Government has the power to remove a member on the grounds of moral turpitude.
questions.e: The term of office for the Chairperson and members is three years, not five. Grounds for removal by the Central Government include being an undischarged insolvent, conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude, or absence from three consecutive meetings without obtaining leave.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a specific function of the National Commission for Minorities as per its nine-point mandate?
o: Looking into specific complaints regarding deprivation of rights and safeguards
Monitoring the working of the safeguards provided in the Constitution
Evaluating the progress of the development of minorities under the Union and States
Providing legal counsel to minority individuals in private civil disputes
questions.e: The Commission's mandate includes evaluating development progress, monitoring constitutional/legal safeguards, and looking into specific complaints of rights deprivation. It does not have a mandate to provide private legal counsel for civil disputes.

questions.q: While inquiring into complaints, the National Commission for Minorities has the powers of which of the following?
questions.e: The Act specifies that the Commission, while evaluating/monitoring matters or inquiring into complaints, has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit.

questions.q: What is the procedure for the submission and processing of the National Commission for Minorities' reports?
o: State-related reports are submitted directly to the Governor
Reports are submitted to the Central Government and then placed before Parliament
The Commission publishes the report without government intervention
The report is submitted to the President of India
questions.e: The Commission presents an annual report to the Central Government, which then places it before each House of Parliament along with a memorandum of action taken. If a report relates to a state matter, a copy is forwarded to that State Government to be placed before the state legislature.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission (CIC) was established under which of the following?
questions.e: The Central Information Commission was established by the Central Government in 2005 under the provisions of the Right to Information Act (2005).

questions.q: With reference to the Central Information Commission (CIC), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a constitutional body. 2️⃣ It looks into complaints and decides appeals pertaining to offices under the Central Government and Union Territories. 3️⃣ It consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners.
questions.e: The CIC is not a constitutional body; it is a statutory body. It consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and a maximum of ten Information Commissioners. It handles complaints/appeals for Central Government and UT offices.

questions.q: Who is part of the committee that recommends the appointment of the Chief Information Commissioner to the President? 1️⃣ Prime Minister 2️⃣ Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha 3️⃣ Chief Justice of India 4️⃣ A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM
questions.e: The committee consists of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The Chief Justice of India is not a member of this specific selection committee.

questions.q: Regarding the tenure of Information Commissioners after the RTI Amendment Act of 2019, which of the following is true?
o: The term is as prescribed by the Central Government
The term is fixed at 3 years
The term is fixed at 5 years
They hold office until the age of 70
questions.e: The RTI Amendment Act of 2019 changed the fixed 5-year term to "such term as prescribed by the Central Government" or until they attain the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: In which case must the President refer the matter to the Supreme Court for an enquiry before removing the Chief Information Commissioner?
o: On the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity
If they are convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude
If they engage in paid employment outside their office
If they are adjudged an insolvent
questions.e: While the President can remove the CIC for insolvency or outside employment directly , removal on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity requires a reference to the Supreme Court for an enquiry.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Central Information Commission: 1️⃣ It has the power to order an inquiry into any matter on reasonable grounds (suo-moto). 2️⃣ During an inquiry, no public record under the control of a public authority can be withheld from it. 3️⃣ It can impose a penalty on a Public Information Officer up to a maximum of ₹25,000.
questions.e: The CIC has suo-moto inquiry powers. All public records must be given to it during an inquiry. It can also impose a penalty of ₹250 per day up to ₹25,000 on errant Public Information Officers.

questions.q: Who recommends the appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: A committee headed by the Governor
A committee headed by the Chief Minister
The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The State Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Chief Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly, and a State Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM.

questions.q: The salaries and service conditions of the State Chief Information Commissioner are prescribed by:
questions.e: Following the RTI Amendment Act of 2019, the salary, allowances, and other service conditions of the State Chief Information Commissioner and State Information Commissioners are prescribed by the Central Government.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the State Information Commission?
o: To appoint Public Information Officers for all state departments
To reverse the decisions of the High Court regarding RTI
To provide legal defense to applicants in court
To recommend disciplinary action against errant officials
questions.e: The State Information Commission has the power to secure compliance, which includes recommending disciplinary action against errant officials. It does not have the power to reverse High Court decisions.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 based on the recommendations of:
questions.e: The establishment of the CVC in 1964 was recommended by the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64).

questions.q: What is the current status of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?
o: It is a private autonomous society
It is a purely Executive body
questions.e: Originally set up by an executive resolution, the CVC was later conferred statutory status by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

questions.q: Who heads the committee that recommends the appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
questions.e: The recommendation committee is a three-member body consisting of the Prime Minister (as head), the Union Minister of Home Affairs, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
questions.e: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and vigilance commissioners hold office for a term of four years or until they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: After their tenure, the Central Vigilance Commissioner is:
o: Not eligible for further employment under the Central or a State government
Eligible for any employment under the State Government
Eligible for reappointment in the same position
Eligible to become an Information Commissioner
questions.e: The Act explicitly states that after their tenure, they are not eligible for further employment under the Central or a state government.

questions.q: The jurisdiction of the CVC includes which of the following? 1️⃣ Members of All India Services serving in the Union. 2️⃣ Group A officers of the Central Government. 3️⃣ Officers of the rank of Scale V and above in Public Sector Banks. 4️⃣ All employees of the State Governments.
questions.e: The CVC's jurisdiction covers All India Service members in the Union, Group A central officers, and specific senior ranks in PSBs, RBI, and PSUs. It does not extend to all state government employees.

questions.q: Which wing of the CVC conducts technical audits of construction works of Government organisations from a vigilance angle?
questions.e: The Chief Technical Examiners' Wing (CTE) is the technical wing of the CVC responsible for technical audits of construction works and investigating complaints related to them.

questions.q: The "Whistle Blowers" Resolution (PIDPI) 2004 designated which agency to receive and act on complaints?
questions.e: The CVC has been designated as the agency to receive and act on complaints under the "Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers' Resolution" (PIDPI), 2004.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Whistle Blowers Protection Act (2014): 1️⃣ It provides a mechanism for protecting the identity of whistle blowers. 2️⃣ It applies to the Special Protection Group (SPG). 3️⃣ It provides for punishment for false or frivolous complaints.
questions.e: The Act protects identities and punishes false complaints. However, it is specifically not applicable to the Special Protection Group.

questions.q: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) derives its powers from:
o: The Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
questions.e: While the CBI was established by a resolution, it is not a statutory body; it derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.

questions.q: Under which Ministry does the CBI function?
questions.e: The CBI functions under the administrative control of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) of the Ministry of Personnel.

questions.q: Who is the Chairperson of the committee that recommends the appointment of the Director of CBI?
questions.e: The appointment is made on the recommendation of a three-member committee consisting of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India (or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by him/her).

questions.q: Regarding the tenure of the Director of CBI, the 2021 amendment allows for extensions up to a total of how many years?
questions.e: Originally a two-year tenure, the 2021 amendment allows the central government to extend the tenure up to five years in total, with annual extensions of one year at a time.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the CBI's jurisdiction is correct?
o: It requires the consent of the State Government to exercise jurisdiction in that State
It only investigates cases within the Union Territory of Delhi
It has no jurisdiction over Central Government employees serving in states
It can investigate any case in any state without local permission
questions.e: The DSPE Act (1946) does not enable the CBI to exercise its powers in a State (excluding railway areas) without the consent of that State's Government.

questions.q: The CBI acts as the "National Central Bureau" for which international organisation in India?
questions.e: The CBI acts as the "National Central Bureau" of Interpol in India, coordinating requests from Indian and international law enforcement agencies.

questions.q: What did the Supreme Court hold in 2014 regarding prior permission for the CBI to probe senior bureaucrats?
o: It is mandatory for all cases
It is valid and necessary for administrative efficiency
It held the legal provision requiring prior sanction as invalid
It is required only for officers above the rank of Secretary
questions.e: In 2014, a Constitution Bench held that Section 6A of the DSPE Act, which required prior sanction for probing senior bureaucrats (joint secretary and above), was violative of Article 14 and thus invalid.

questions.q: The institution of 'Ombudsman' was first created in which country?
questions.e: The earliest democratic institution of Ombudsman was created in Sweden in 1809 to handle complaints against administrative and judicial action.

questions.q: In the socialist countries like the former USSR and China, the institutional device for redressal of citizens' grievances is called:
questions.e: The socialist countries use the 'Procurator System' for the redressal of citizens' grievances.

questions.q: Which Indian Prime Minister's government introduced the first Lokpal Bill in Parliament?
questions.e: The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in May 1968 by the Congress Government headed by Indira Gandhi.

questions.q: With reference to the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act (2013), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and a maximum of 8 members. 2️⃣ 50% of the members must be judicial members. 3️⃣ The Prime Minister is completely excluded from the jurisdiction of Lokpal.
questions.e: The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and up to 8 members, with 50% being judicial members. The Prime Minister is actually brought under the purview of the Lokpal, though with certain subject matter exclusions.

questions.q: Who nominates the "eminent jurist" in the selection committee for Lokpal?
questions.e: The eminent jurist is nominated by the President of India based on the recommendations of the first four members of the selection committee (PM, Speaker, LoP, and CJI).

questions.q: What is the timeline for a preliminary enquiry by Lokpal?
o: Six months extendable by six months
Three months extendable by three months
One month extendable by one month
questions.e: The Act lays down a timeline of three months for a preliminary enquiry, which is extendable by another three months.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a drawback of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: It cannot suo motu proceed against any public servant
It has too many members from the ruling party
It does not cover Group A and B officers
questions.e: One of the listed drawbacks is that the Lokpal cannot initiate proceedings against a public servant on its own (suo motu). It also does not allow anonymous complaints.

questions.q: Which state was the first to establish the institution of Lokayukta?
questions.e: While Odisha passed the Act in 1970, the institution of Lokayukta was established first in Maharashtra in 1971.

questions.q: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) was established primarily in response to:
questions.e: The NIA was established in 2009 in the backdrop of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks (26/11 incident) to deal with terror-related crimes.

questions.q: The NIA works under the administrative control of which Ministry?
questions.e: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) works under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

questions.q: Which amendment empowered the NIA to investigate offences committed outside India against Indian citizens?
questions.e: The NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019 applied the provisions of the Act to persons who commit scheduled offences beyond India against Indian citizens or interests.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).

questions.q: What is the maximum number of members in the NDMA, excluding the chairperson?
questions.e: The NDMA consists of a chairperson and other members, not exceeding nine.

questions.q: Which force is under the general superintendence and control of the NDMA?
questions.e: The NDMA exercises general superintendence, direction, and control over the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF).

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)?
questions.e: The Collector (or District Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner) of the district is the ex-officio chairperson of the DDMA.

questions.q: The Bar Council of India (BCI) is a statutory body established under:
questions.e: The Bar Council of India was established under the Advocates Act, 1961, making it a statutory body.

questions.q: Who are the ex-officio members of the Bar Council of India?
o: Attorney-General of India and Solicitor-General of India
President of the Supreme Court Bar Association
Chief Justice of India and Law Minister
questions.e: The Attorney-General of India and the Solicitor-General of India are the ex-officio members of the BCI.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Chairman and Vice-Chairman of the Bar Council of India?
questions.e: The Chairman and Vice-Chairman of the BCI are elected by the Council from among its members and hold office for a period of two years.

questions.q: Which category of advocate is entitled to act and plead for a party in the Supreme Court?
questions.e: No advocate other than an Advocate-on-Record is entitled to file an appearance or act for a party in the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The Law Commission of India is which type of body?
questions.e: The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory advisory body established by the order of the Central Government for a fixed tenure.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the First Law Commission of independent India?
questions.e: The first Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955 and was headed by M.C. Setalvad, the then Attorney-General of India.

questions.q: What is the usual term for a Law Commission of India?
questions.e: The Law Commission is established from time to time, usually with a three-year term.

questions.q: The 22nd Law Commission of India was headed by:
questions.e: The 22nd Law Commission of India, constituted in 2020, was headed by Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi.

questions.q: Which pre-independence Law Commission was headed by Lord Macaulay?
questions.e: The First Law Commission during the British regime was established in 1834 with Lord Macaulay as its Chairman.

questions.q: Which functionary belongs to the Indian Legal Service and holds the rank of Additional Secretary/Secretary in the Law Commission?
questions.e: The Member-Secretary of the Law Commission belongs to the Indian Legal Service and holds the rank of either Additional Secretary or Secretary to the Government of India.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 21st Law Commission (2015-2018): 1️⃣ It submitted a report on "Hate Speech". 2️⃣ It reviewed the "Contempt of Courts Act, 1971". 3️⃣ It recommended the "Compulsory Registration of Marriages".
questions.e: All three topics were subjects of reports submitted by the 21st Law Commission: Report No. 267 on Hate Speech, Report No. 270 on Compulsory Registration of Marriages, and Report No. 274 on the Contempt of Courts Act.

questions.q: The State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) consists of how many members including the chairperson?
questions.e: An SDMA consists of a chairperson and other members, not exceeding nine. Since the CM is the chairperson and there are up to nine "other" members, the total can be up to ten.

questions.q: In Tribal Areas (Sixth Schedule), who is the ex-officio co-chairperson of the DDMA?
o: Chief Executive Member of the district council
Elected representative of the local authority
questions.e: In Tribal Areas referred to in the Sixth Schedule, the chief executive member of the district council of the autonomous district is the ex-officio co-chairperson of the DDMA.

questions.q: Regarding the Central Information Commission, what is the age limit for holding office?
questions.e: The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners hold office until they attain the age of 65 years.

questions.q: The NIA TFFC Cell specifically deals with which of the following?
questions.e: The NIA has a separate specialised cell known as the TFFC Cell dealing with fake currency notes and terror funding.

questions.q: Which body was established in 1964 to monitor all vigilance activity under the Central Government?
questions.e: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 as the apex vigilance institution to monitor vigilance activity under the Central Government.

questions.q: The salary of the Chief Information Commissioner, prior to the 2019 amendment, was similar to:
questions.e: Before the 2019 amendment, the salary and service conditions of the Chief Information Commissioner were similar to those of the Chief Election Commissioner.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a committee of the Bar Council of India?
questions.e: The BCI consists of several committees including Disciplinary, Legal Aid, Executive, and Legal Education Committees. A "Judicial Review Committee" is not mentioned.

questions.q: The motto of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is:
questions.e: The motto of the CBI is "Industry, Impartiality and Integrity".

questions.q: Who recommended the establishment of an All India Bar Council in 1953?
questions.e: In 1951, the All India Bar Committee under Justice S.R. Das was appointed, and it recommended the establishment of the BCI in its 1953 report.

questions.q: The State Information Commission submits its annual report to:
questions.e: The State Information Commission submits an annual report to the State Government on the implementation of the Act's provisions.

questions.q: How many religious communities are currently notified as minorities in India as per the Act?
questions.e: Five communities were notified in 1993 (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Zoroastrians), and Jains were added in 2014, making a total of six.

questions.q: Which of the following can remove a member of the National Commission for Minorities on the ground of "moral turpitude"?
questions.e: The Central Government has the power to remove the Chairperson or a member if they are convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude.

questions.q: The "File to Field" programme, where administrators hear public grievances in villages, is an innovative scheme in which state?
questions.e: The "File to Field" programme is an innovative grievance redressal scheme mentioned as being used in some states like Kerala.

questions.q: What is the punishment for false or frivolous complaints under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act?
o: Up to 3 years prison and ₹50,000 fine
Up to 2 years prison and ₹30,000 fine
Up to 1 year prison and ₹10,000 fine
No punishment, only dismissal of case
questions.e: The Act lays down a punishment of up to two years in prison and a fine of up to ₹30,000 for false or frivolous complaints.

questions.q: Which body acts as the district planning and implementing body for disaster management?
questions.e: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) acts as the district planning, coordinating, and implementing body for disaster management.

questions.q: Regarding the Director of Prosecution in CBI, which of the following is true?
o: He/she functions under the overall supervision of the Director of CBI
He/she is appointed by the Chief Justice of India
He/she is appointed by the Prime Minister
He/she is the same person as the Director of CBI
questions.e: The Directorate of Prosecution is headed by a Director who functions under the overall supervision and control of the Director of CBI.

questions.q: The term of office for a member of the BCI elected by a State Bar Council is:
o: Linked to their tenure in the State Bar Council
questions.e: The term of office of a member of the BCI elected by an SBC is the period for which he/she holds office as a member of that SBC.

questions.q: Which pre-independence Law Commission recommended the Indian Penal Code?
questions.e: The Indian Penal Code is one of the products of the first four pre-independence Law Commissions, with the First Law Commission (1834) specifically chaired by Lord Macaulay who drafted it.

questions.q: The National Commission for Minorities is under the administrative control of:
questions.e: The Commission works under the administrative control of the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India.

questions.q: What is the limitation period for filing a complaint with the Lokpal?
questions.e: One of the drawbacks mentioned is the limitation period of 7 years to file complaints with the Lokpal.

questions.q: Who designates the Vice-Chairperson of the NDMA?
questions.e: The Prime Minister, as the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA, nominates the other members and designates one of them as the vice-chairperson.

questions.q: The salary of a State Information Commissioner, after the 2019 amendment, is similar to:
o: As prescribed by the Central Government
As prescribed by the State Government
The Chief Secretary of the state
questions.e: Before 2019, it was similar to the Chief Secretary, but the amendment provided that their salary and service conditions shall be such as prescribed by the Central Government.

questions.q: Which wing of the CBI was merged into it in 1963?
questions.e: In 1963, when the CBI was established, the Delhi Special Police Establishment was merged with it and made one of its divisions.

questions.q: The Scandinavian institution of 'Ombudsman' refers to a person who acts as:
o: The representative or spokesman of another person
questions.e: 'Ombud' is a Swedish term referring to a person who acts as the representative or spokesman of another person.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio member of every State Bar Council?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: In the case of any State Bar Council, the Advocate-General of the state is the ex-officio member.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a ground for removal of the Central Vigilance Commissioner by the President?
o: Engaging in paid employment outside office
questions.e: Grounds for removal include insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, outside employment, or being unfit due to infirmity, but not disagreement with government policy.

questions.q: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has jurisdiction over:
questions.e: In 2019, NIA's jurisdiction was extended to include human trafficking, counterfeit currency, prohibited arms, and cyber-terrorism.

questions.q: The "eminent jurist" in the Lokpal Selection Committee is nominated by the President on the recommendation of:
o: The first four members of the selection committee
questions.e: The eminent jurist is nominated by the President on the basis of recommendations of the first four members: PM, Speaker, LoP, and CJI (or nominee).

questions.q: Which report of the Law Commission dealt with "Wrongful Prosecution (Miscarriage of Justice)"?
questions.e: Report No. 277, submitted by the 21st Law Commission in 2018, was titled "Wrongful Prosecution (Miscarriage of Justice): Legal Remedies".

questions.q: The Central Information Commission consists of how many Information Commissioners besides the Chief?
questions.e: The Commission consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners.

questions.q: Who designates the Vice-Chairperson of the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)?
o: The Cabinet Minister nominated by CM
questions.e: The Chief Minister, as the chairperson of the SDMA, designates one of the members as the vice-chairperson.

questions.q: The Bar Council of India has the power to recognize universities whose degree in law shall be a qualification for:
questions.e: One of BCI's functions is to recognize universities whose law degree qualifies a person for enrolment as an advocate.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Chairperson and members of the National Commission for Minorities?
questions.e: The chairperson and members of the National Commission for Minorities hold office for a period of three years.

questions.q: In which state is the National Institute of Disaster Management located?
questions.e: The National Institute of Disaster Management is located in New Delhi.

questions.q: The CBI requires prior approval of the Central Government for investigating officers of which rank?
questions.e: The CBI was required to obtain prior approval for officers of the rank of joint secretary and above, though the Supreme Court later struck this down in corruption cases.

questions.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Chief Executive Officer of the State Disaster Management Authority?
o: The Chairperson of the State Executive Committee
questions.e: The chairperson of the State Executive Committee acts as the ex-officio chief executive officer of the SDMA.

questions.q: The 22nd Law Commission's term was extended until:
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved the extension of the term of the 22nd Law Commission up to 31st August, 2024.

questions.q: Which function of the Lokayukta is common in almost all states?
o: Including Ministers and higher civil servants in its purview
Including the Judiciary in its purview
Including the Chief Minister in its purview
questions.e: While jurisdiction over the CM varies, ministers and higher civil servants are included in the purview of lokayukta in almost all states.

questions.q: The Bar Council of India's Legal Education Committee is one of its:
questions.e: The Legal Education Committee is listed as one of the specific committees within the Bar Council of India.

questions.q: What status does the Vice-Chairperson of the NDMA hold?
questions.e: The vice-chairperson of the NDMA has the status of a Cabinet Minister, while other members have the status of a Minister of State.

questions.q: Which agency is designated to take action against complainants making motivated or vexatious complaints under PIDPI?
questions.e: The CVC is empowered as the only designated agency to take action against complainants making motivated or vexatious complaints.

questions.q: The NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019 allows for the designation of which courts as Special Courts?
questions.e: The amendment provided that the central and state governments may designate Sessions Courts as Special Courts for conducting trials of offences under the NIA Act.

questions.q: Regarding the historical background of the Law Commission, how many Law Commissions were established during the British regime in the 19th century?
questions.e: During the British regime, four Law Commissions were established in the 19th century. These commissions made significant contributions to the Indian Statute Book by recommending legislations like the IPC and the Indian Evidence Act.

questions.q: Which of the following acts is a product of the four pre-independence Law Commissions? 1️⃣ The Indian Contract Act 2️⃣ The Indian Evidence Act 3️⃣ The Transfer of Property Act 4️⃣ The Civil Procedure Code
questions.e: The Indian Penal Code, Criminal Procedure Code, Civil Procedure Code, Indian Contract Act, Indian Evidence Act, and the Transfer of Property Act are all products of the first four pre-independence Law Commissions.

questions.q: With reference to the first Law Commission of independent India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was established in 1955. 2️⃣ Its term was fixed for five years. 3️⃣ It was headed by M.C. Setalvad.
questions.e: The First Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955 for a three-year term. It was headed by M.C. Setalvad, who was the Attorney-General of India at that time.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the 21st Law Commission of India (2015-2018)?
questions.e: The 21st Law Commission, which served from 2015 to 2018, was chaired by Justice B.S. Chauhan.

questions.q: Which official serves as the Member-Secretary of the Law Commission of India?
o: An eminent member of the Bar
A professor of law from a National Law University
An official from the Indian Legal Service
questions.e: The Member-Secretary of the Law Commission belongs to the Indian Legal Service and holds the rank of either Additional Secretary or Secretary to the Government of India.

questions.q: Regarding the working process of the Law Commission, what is the purpose of a "working paper"?
o: It is a document outlining problems and suggested reforms for public circulation
It is the final report sent to the President
It is a list of members' attendance records
It is a secret document for the Ministry of Law and Justice only
questions.e: A working paper emerges as an outcome of preparatory work to outline problems and suggest reforms. It is then circulated to the public and interest groups to elicit reactions and suggestions.

questions.q: The final report of the Law Commission is forwarded to which specific authority?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Ministry of Law and Justice
questions.e: After the report is finalized by the full Commission, it is forwarded to the Government, specifically the Ministry of Law and Justice.

questions.q: As of the information provided in the text, how many reports has the Law Commission submitted in total?
questions.e: Till the time of the writing of the provided text, the Commission had submitted 277 reports on various legal subjects.

questions.q: Which Law Commission report focused on the "Assessment of Statutory Framework of Tribunals in India"?
questions.e: Report No. 272, submitted in 2017, dealt with the Assessment of the Statutory Framework of Tribunals in India.

questions.q: Which body serves as the main agency for preventing corruption in the Central Government?
questions.e: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is established as the main agency for preventing corruption within the Central Government.

questions.q: In 2014, which community was added to the list of notified minority communities in India?
questions.e: In 2014, the Jain community was added to the list of minority communities, joining Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, and Zoroastrians.

questions.q: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was carved out of which Ministry in 2006?
questions.e: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was created in 2006 by carving it out from the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment.

questions.q: According to the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, who has the power to notify a community as a 'minority'?
questions.e: The Act does not define 'minority' but enables the Central Government to notify communities as minorities for the purposes of the Act.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of members a State Bar Council can have based on its electorate size?
questions.e: In the case of an SBC with an electorate of more than ten thousand, it consists of 25 members. Smaller electorates have 15 or 20 members.

questions.q: For how many years must a person have been an advocate on a state roll to make up one-half of the elected members of a State Bar Council?
questions.e: One-half of the elected members of a State Bar Council must be persons who have been advocates on a state roll for ten years.

questions.q: Which official is an ex-officio member of the Bar Council of Delhi?
o: The Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court
questions.e: In the case of the State Bar Council of Delhi, the Additional Solicitor-General of India is an ex-officio member.

questions.q: What is the term of office for an elected member of any State Bar Council?
questions.e: The term of office for an elected member of any State Bar Council is fixed at five years.

questions.q: Which committee is NOT specifically listed as a mandatory committee for a State Bar Council?
questions.e: While the BCI has a Legal Education Committee, the State Bar Councils are listed as having Disciplinary, Legal Aid, Executive, and Enrolment committees.

questions.q: Under the Advocates Act, 1961, who has the power to designate an advocate as a 'Senior Advocate'?
o: The Supreme Court or a High Court
The Ministry of Law and Justice
questions.e: An advocate may be designated as a senior advocate if the Supreme Court or a High Court is of the opinion that they deserve such distinction due to their ability or special knowledge.

questions.q: Which of the following is a restriction on a 'Senior Advocate' in the Supreme Court?
o: They are not entitled to appear without an Advocate-on-Record
They cannot take up criminal cases
questions.e: A Senior Advocate is not entitled to appear in the Supreme Court without an Advocate-on-Record.

questions.q: How many years of training must an advocate receive from a senior Advocate-on-Record to be eligible for the AOR examination?
questions.e: To be eligible for the AOR examination, an advocate must have received training from an Advocate-on-Record of at least ten years standing for a continuous period of one year.

questions.q: Which state bar council covers the Union Territory of Lakshadweep?
o: Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa
questions.e: The Bar Council of Kerala has jurisdiction over both the state of Kerala and the Union Territory of Lakshadweep.

questions.q: The Bar Council of West Bengal also covers which Union Territory?
questions.e: The Bar Council of West Bengal covers West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.q: In the context of the NDMA, what is the status of the "other members" nominated by the chairperson?
questions.e: While the vice-chairperson of the NDMA has the status of a Cabinet Minister, the other members have the status of a Minister of State.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for approving the "National Plan" for disaster management?
questions.e: One of the primary functions of the NDMA is to approve the National Plan for disaster management.

questions.q: Who acts as the ex-officio co-chairperson of the DDMA in a district where a Zilla Parishad exists?
o: The Chairperson of the Zilla Parishad
questions.e: In districts where a Zilla Parishad exists, its chairperson acts as the co-chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA).

questions.q: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, which authority is responsible for organizing specialized training for voluntary rescue workers in the district?
questions.e: The DDMA is tasked with organizing and coordinating specialized training programs for officers, employees, and voluntary rescue workers at the district level.

questions.q: The NIA was established after which major event?
questions.e: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) was established in 2009 in the backdrop of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks (26/11).

questions.q: Which of the following is a "Scheduled Offence" that the NIA is empowered to probe? 1️⃣ Human trafficking 2️⃣ Counterfeit currency 3️⃣ Cyber-terrorism 4️⃣ Hijacking of aircrafts
questions.e: The NIA probes terror attacks, hijacking, and attacks on nuclear installations. Since 2019, its jurisdiction also includes human trafficking, counterfeit currency, and cyber-terrorism.

questions.q: Regarding the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act (2013), what percentage of members must come from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities, and women?
questions.e: The Act mandates that 50% of the members of the Lokpal must come from amongst the SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities, and women.

questions.q: Who assists the Selection Committee in the process of selecting the Lokpal chairperson and members?
questions.e: A Search Committee assists the Selection Committee in the selection process, and 50% of its members must also be from reserved categories.

questions.q: If a complaint is referred to the CVC by the Lokpal regarding Group C and D employees, what is the procedure?
o: The Lokpal conducts the inquiry directly
The case is transferred to the CBI immediately
The CVC proceeds in exercise of its own powers subject to Lokpal's review
The CVC sends a report back to Lokpal for a decision
questions.e: For Group C and D employees, the CVC proceeds under its own powers but remains subject to reporting and review by the Lokpal.

questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 enhanced the maximum punishment under the Prevention of Corruption Act to how many years?
questions.e: The Act increased the maximum punishment under the Prevention of Corruption Act from seven years to ten years.

questions.q: Which entity is specifically EXCLUDED from the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: Institutions financed partly by the Government
Institutions financed fully by the Government
questions.e: While institutions financed fully or partly by the Government fall under Lokpal's jurisdiction, those merely "aided" by the Government are excluded.

questions.q: Entities receiving foreign donations in excess of what amount per year under FCRA are brought under Lokpal's jurisdiction?
questions.e: All entities receiving donations from foreign sources in excess of ₹10 lakhs per year under FCRA are subject to the Lokpal.

questions.q: Within how many days of the commencement of the Lokpal Act were states mandated to set up the institution of Lokayukta?
questions.e: The Act contained a mandate for states to set up the institution of Lokayukta through state law within 365 days.

questions.q: The "Procurator System" is the grievance redressal institutional device in which country?
questions.e: Socialist countries like Russia (former USSR) and China use the 'Procurator System' for citizens' grievances.

questions.q: According to Donald C. Rowat, what is the Ombudsman system described as?
o: A legal hurdle for the executive
A bulwark of democratic government against the tyranny of officialdom
questions.e: Donald C. Rowat famously described the Ombudsman as a "bulwark of democratic government against the tyranny of officialdom".

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Central Information Commission?
o: Drafting new amendments to the RTI Act
Providing access to information in a particular form
questions.e: The CIC's powers include providing access, imposing penalties, and rejecting applications, but it does not have the legislative function of drafting amendments to the Act.

questions.q: The Chief Information Commissioner can be removed by the President on the ground of "infirmity of mind or body". In this specific case, is a Supreme Court enquiry required?
o: No, only in cases of misbehaviour or incapacity
Yes, if the Cabinet recommends it
Only if the Commissioner challenges the decision
questions.e: For grounds like insolvency, outside employment, or infirmity of mind/body, the President can remove the Commissioner directly . The Supreme Court reference is mandatory only for "proved misbehaviour or incapacity".

questions.q: In the absence of a recognized Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, who takes their place in the CIC selection committee?
o: The Leader of the single largest opposition group
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Whip of the largest party
questions.e: If no Leader of Opposition is recognized, the Leader of the single largest group in opposition in the Lok Sabha is deemed to be the Leader of the Opposition for selection purposes.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 1978 Minorities Commission is correct?
o: It was established by the Supreme Court
It was set up by an executive resolution
It was a statutory body from the start
questions.e: The Minorities Commission was initially set up in 1978 via an executive resolution to safeguard the interests of minorities.

questions.q: Which community was notified as a minority community in India on 27th January, 2014?
questions.e: The Jain community was added to the list of minority communities through a notification dated 27th January, 2014.

questions.q: What was the composition of the National Commission for Minorities before the 1995 Amendment Act?
questions.e: Before the Amendment Act of 1995, the Commission consisted of a Chairperson and six members.

questions.q: Who prescribes the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and members of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: The Central Government (Ministry of Minority Affairs)
questions.e: The Central Government, specifically the Ministry of Minority Affairs, prescribes the salaries, allowances, and service conditions for the Commission.

questions.q: If a member of the National Commission for Minorities becomes an "undischarged insolvent," they can be removed by?
questions.e: The Central Government has the power to remove the Chairperson or a member under circumstances such as becoming an undischarged insolvent.

questions.q: When the National Commission for Minorities forwards a report to a State Government, the state must place it before?
questions.e: The State Government is required to place the Commission's report before the state legislature along with a memorandum explaining action taken or reasons for non-acceptance.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission entertains complaints and appeals relating to which of the following?
o: Offices and PSUs under the Central Government
questions.e: The CIC's jurisdiction covers offices, financial institutions, and public sector undertakings under the Central Government and Union Territories.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a qualification for appointment as an Information Commissioner?
o: Being a sitting Member of Parliament
questions.e: Information Commissioners must be persons of eminence but should not be a Member of Parliament or a Member of the Legislature of any State or UT.

questions.q: An Information Commissioner is eligible for appointment as Chief Information Commissioner, but their total term cannot exceed how many years?
questions.e: An Information Commissioner can become the Chief, but their total combined term in both offices cannot exceed five years.

questions.q: What rate of penalty can the Central Information Commission impose on a Public Information Officer?
questions.e: The Commission can impose a penalty of ₹250 per day, up to a maximum of ₹25,000, on an errant PIO.

questions.q: The State Information Commission consists of a State Chief Information Commissioner and how many State Information Commissioners?
questions.e: The State Commission consists of a State Chief and not more than ten State Information Commissioners.

questions.q: In the State Information Commission, who nominates the State Cabinet Minister for the selection committee?
questions.e: The selection committee includes a State Cabinet Minister who is nominated by the Chief Minister.

questions.q: If the State Chief Information Commissioner is concerned with a contract made by the State Government, they are deemed guilty of?
questions.e: A Commissioner is deemed guilty of misbehaviour if they are interested in any contract or agreement made by the State Government.

questions.q: Which amendment removed the provision regarding deductions in salary due to pension for Information Commissioners?
questions.e: The RTI Amendment Act of 2019 removed provisions that allowed for salary deductions based on pensions or retirement benefits received from previous government service.

questions.q: originally, the Central Vigilance Commission was?
o: A wing of the Supreme Court
Neither a constitutional nor a statutory body
questions.e: Originally, the CVC was an executive body and was neither constitutional nor statutory. It gained statutory status in 2003.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and how many vigilance commissioners?
questions.e: The CVC is a multi-member body with a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two vigilance commissioners.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the President by:
o: Warrant under his hand and seal
questions.e: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and vigilance commissioners are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.q: The salary and service conditions of the Central Vigilance Commissioner are similar to:
questions.e: The service conditions of the Central Vigilance Commissioner are similar to those of the Chairman of the UPSC.

questions.q: Which wing of the CVC conducts oral inquiries in departmental proceedings against public servants?
questions.e: The Commissioners for Departmental Inquiries (CDIs) function as inquiry officers for oral inquiries in departmental proceedings.

questions.q: The CVC exercises superintendence over the CBI (Delhi Special Police Establishment) for investigations under which Act?
questions.e: The CVC's superintendence over the CBI is specifically for investigations related to offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

questions.q: Officers of which rank in Public Sector Banks fall under CVC jurisdiction?
questions.e: The CVC's jurisdiction includes officers of the rank of Scale V and above in Public Sector Banks.

questions.q: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was originally numbered as which year's Act?
questions.e: Originally, the year of the Whistle Blowers Protection Act was 2011, though it was later changed to 2014.

questions.q: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, a disclosure must contain:
o: Only the name of the accused
questions.e: No action is taken on a disclosure if it does not indicate the identity of the complainant.

questions.q: The CBI traces its origin to which establishment set up in 1941?
questions.e: The CBI originated from the Special Police Establishment set up by the Government of India in 1941.

questions.q: Which Ministry was the CBI originally established under in 1963?
questions.e: The CBI was established in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs. It was later transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

questions.q: In the CBI's selection committee, who can nominate a Supreme Court Judge to replace them?
questions.e: The selection committee for the Director of CBI includes the Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court nominated by him/her.

questions.q: The Director of Prosecution in CBI is appointed on the recommendation of?
questions.e: The Director of Prosecution in the CBI is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of the CVC.

questions.q: Who assists the Director of CBI in the administration of the organization?
questions.e: The Director of CBI is assisted by special directors and additional directors in managing the organisation.

questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act (2013) amended which 1946 Act?
questions.e: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act (2013) made several amendments to the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act (1946).

questions.q: Which body coordinates requests for investigation-related activities originating from member countries of Interpol?
questions.e: The Interpol Wing of the CBI coordinates investigation requests between Indian law enforcement and Interpol member countries.

questions.q: The Supreme Court ruled that Section 6A of the DSPE Act was violative of which Article of the Constitution?
questions.e: The Supreme Court held Section 6A of the DSPE Act invalid because it violated Article 14 (Right to Equality).

questions.q: When there is a conflict between DSPE and state police, which agency takes up cases substantially concerned with the state government's affairs?
questions.e: Administrative arrangements state that the state police force shall take up cases substantially concerned with the state government's affairs.

questions.q: The earliest democratic institution of the 'Ombudsman' was created in Sweden in which year?
questions.e: Sweden was the first country to create the institution of the Ombudsman in 1809.

questions.q: Which scholar described the Ombudsman as "institutionalised public conscience"?
questions.e: Scholar Gerald E. Caiden described the Ombudsman system as "institutionalised public conscience".

questions.q: The French system for the redressal of citizens' grievances is called:
questions.e: France created a unique institutional device called Administrative Courts for redressing grievances.

questions.q: The First Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) of India (1966-1970) was headed by:
questions.e: The First ARC, which recommended setting up Lokpal and Lokayukta, was headed by Morarji Desai.

questions.q: According to the first ARC, the Lokpal should deal with complaints against which officials?
o: Ministers and Secretaries at Central and state levels
questions.e: The first ARC recommended that the Lokpal deal with complaints against high-level officials like ministers and secretaries.

questions.q: Which state passed the Lokayukta Act in 1970, even before Maharashtra?
questions.e: While Maharashtra established the institution first in 1971, Odisha had passed the relevant Act earlier in 1970.

questions.q: In most states, the term of office fixed for Lokayukta is:
questions.e: Most states have a fixed term of 5 years or until the age of 65 for the Lokayukta.

questions.q: The recommendations made by the lokayukta to the state government are:
questions.e: The recommendations of the lokayukta are advisory and not binding on the state government.

questions.q: The National Investigation Agency Act was passed in which year?
questions.e: The NIA was constituted in 2009 under the provisions of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.

questions.q: Who appoints the Director-General of the NIA?
questions.e: The Director-General of the NIA is appointed by the central government.

questions.q: Which commission made recommendations for establishing a central agency like the NIA?
questions.e: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (headed by Veerappa Moily) recommended establishing a central agency for terror investigation.

questions.q: The NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019 applied to persons who commit offences beyond India against:
questions.e: The 2019 amendment extended NIA jurisdiction to offences committed outside India if they affect Indian citizens or interests.

questions.q: Following the 2004 tsunami, which Act was passed for disaster management?
questions.e: The Disaster Management Act was enacted in 2005 as a defining step following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.

questions.q: Initially, the NDMA was constituted in 2005 by:
questions.e: Before being notified under the Act in 2006, the NDMA was initially set up in 2005 by an Executive Order.

questions.q: Which Ministry provides administrative control to the NDMA?
questions.e: The NDMA works under the administrative control of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)?
o: The Home Minister of the State
questions.e: The Chief Minister of the state serves as the ex-officio chairperson of the SDMA.

questions.q: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) consists of how many members besides the chairperson?
questions.e: A DDMA consists of a chairperson and other members, not exceeding seven.

questions.q: The Bar Council of India (BCI) works under which department of the Ministry of Law and Justice?
questions.e: The BCI works under the Department of Legal Affairs of the Union Ministry of Law and Justice.

questions.q: One member of the BCI is elected by:
questions.e: Each State Bar Council elects one member from amongst its members to the Bar Council of India.

questions.q: Which pre-independence Law Commission was headed by Dr. Whitney Stokes?
questions.e: Dr. Whitney Stokes was the Chairman of the Fourth Law Commission established in 1879.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides that pre-Constitution laws shall remain in force until amended or repealed?
questions.e: Article 372 provides for the continuation of pre-Constitution laws until they are formally amended or repealed.

questions.q: The 22nd Law Commission was constituted in which month and year?
questions.e: The 22nd Law Commission of India was constituted on 21st February, 2020.

questions.q: Which Law Commission report dealt with "Legal Framework: Gambling and Sports Betting"?
questions.e: Report No. 276, submitted in 2018, focused on the legal framework for gambling and sports betting, including in cricket.

questions.q: The term of a member of the National Commission for Minorities is:
questions.e: The chairperson and members of the National Commission for Minorities hold office for a period of three years.

questions.q: Who can refer a matter of misbehaviour by a Central Information Commissioner to the Supreme Court?
questions.e: The President must refer cases of proved misbehaviour or incapacity to the Supreme Court for enquiry.

questions.q: In the state of Goa, which State Bar Council has jurisdiction?
o: Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa
questions.e: Goa is covered by the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa.

questions.q: The Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption functioned during which years?
questions.e: The Santhanam Committee, which recommended the CVC, functioned from 1962 to 1964.

questions.q: The RTI Amendment Act, 2019 changed the term of the State Chief Information Commissioner from:
o: 5 years to such term as prescribed by Central Government
questions.e: Before the 2019 amendment, the term was fixed at 5 years; it is now as prescribed by the Central Government.

questions.q: The NIA DG has powers similar to which official in a state?
questions.e: The Director-General of the NIA exercises powers similar to those of a Director-General of Police in a state.

questions.q: Which body recommends provision of funds for mitigation of disasters to the central government?
questions.e: One of the functions of the NDMA is to recommend the provision of funds for mitigation.

questions.q: How many State Bar Councils are currently in existence according to the text?
questions.e: According to the text, there are currently 24 State Bar Councils.

questions.q: A member of the National Commission for Minorities can resign by addressing their resignation to:
questions.e: Members of the Commission can relinquish their office at any time by addressing their resignation to the Central Government.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission submitted its 2021 report to the Central Government. This report must be placed before:
questions.e: The Central Government is required to place the Commission's annual report before each House of Parliament.

questions.q: Which community's addition to the minority list was notified through a Ministry of Minority Affairs notification dated 27th January, 2014?
questions.e: The notification dated 27th January, 2014, added the Jain community to the list of minorities.

questions.q: The first Commonwealth country to adopt the Ombudsman system was:
questions.e: New Zealand was the first Commonwealth country to adopt the system in 1962.

questions.q: The CBI was transferred from the Ministry of Home Affairs to which Ministry?
questions.e: Later after its establishment, the CBI was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

questions.q: Which body is described as "free of control from any executive authority" in its advisory role?
questions.e: The CVC is conceived to be the apex vigilance institution, free of control from any executive authority.

questions.q: The 21st Law Commission report on "Hate Speech" was which number?
questions.e: Report No. 267 focused on "The Hate Speech".

questions.q: The State Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The Governor makes the appointment on the recommendation of the selection committee.

questions.q: The NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019 empowered the Central Government to direct the NIA to register cases committed:
o: Outside India as if they took place in India
questions.e: The amendment allows the NIA to investigate offences committed outside India as if they occurred in India.

questions.q: Which rank of officers drawing salary of ₹8700/- per month and above on Central D.A. pattern fall under CVC jurisdiction?
o: Officers in societies and local authorities owned by Central Government
questions.e: CVC jurisdiction includes specific salary-based categories in societies and local authorities owned by the Central Government.

questions.q: The term of a Senior Advocate in the BCI Permanent Committee is not specified, but who is the Chairperson of this committee?
questions.e: The Chief Justice of India is the Chairperson of the Permanent Committee dealing with Senior Advocate designations.

questions.q: Which Act transferring the Special Police Establishment to the Home Department was brought into force in 1946?
questions.e: The DSPE Act, 1946 transferred the superintendence of the SPE to the Home Department.

questions.q: The 2019 RTI amendment provided that the salary of the State Chief Information Commissioner shall be prescribed by:
questions.e: The Central Government now prescribes the salary and service conditions for State Information Commissioners.

questions.q: The Scandinavian countries that adopted the Ombudsman after Sweden include Denmark in which year?
questions.e: Denmark adopted the system in 1955.

questions.q: Who recommends the appointment of the Director of Prosecution in CBI?
questions.e: The CVC recommends the appointment of the Director of Prosecution.

questions.q: In Sweden, does the Ombudsman have the power to reverse an administrative decision?
questions.e: The Swedish Ombudsman has no power to reverse or quash a decision.

questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act (2013) provides for special courts to achieve trials within what timeline?
questions.e: Special courts are set up to achieve a trial period of one year, extendable by one more year.

questions.q: Which body is the apex body for disaster management in India?
questions.e: The NDMA is the apex body for disaster management in the country.

questions.q: The BCI can establish funds for which purpose? 1️⃣ Welfare schemes for indigent advocates 2️⃣ Giving legal aid or advice 3️⃣ Establishing law libraries
questions.e: The BCI can establish funds for advocate welfare, legal aid, and law libraries

questions.q: Which pre-independence Law Commission was chaired by Sir John Romilly?
questions.e: Sir John Romilly was the Chairman of both the Second (1853) and Third (1861) Law Commissions.

questions.q: The 22nd Law Commission's Chairman and members were appointed in which month and year?
questions.e: Although constituted in 2020, the appointments were made in November 2022.

questions.q: Which Law Commission report focused on "Human DNA Profiling"?
questions.e: Report No. 271 dealt with Human DNA Profiling and a draft bill for DNA technology regulation.

questions.q: The term of a member of the CIC, before the 2019 amendment, was fixed for how many years?
questions.e: Prior to the 2019 amendment, the term was fixed at 5 years.

questions.q: Which body has all the powers of a civil court and its proceedings have a judicial character?
questions.e: The CVC is vested with civil court powers and its proceedings are of a judicial character.

questions.q: The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was constituted in which year?
questions.e: The first statutory Commission was constituted in 1993 following the 1992 Act.

questions.q: Who appoints the chief executive officer of the DDMA?
questions.e: The chief executive officer of the DDMA is appointed by the state government.

questions.q: Which Law Commission report reviewed the "Contempt of Courts Act, 1971"?
questions.e: Report No. 274 was titled "Review of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971".

questions.q: The NIA has concurrent jurisdiction to investigate offences affecting:
o: The sovereignty, security, and integrity of India
questions.e: The NIA has jurisdiction over offences affecting India's sovereignty and security.

questions.q: The salaries of the Chairman and members of the Minorities Commission are prescribed by:
questions.e: The Ministry of Minority Affairs prescribes these conditions.

questions.q: Which scholar called the Ombudsman a "uniquely appropriate institution"?
questions.e: Donald C. Rowat used this description for the Ombudsman system.

questions.q: The CBI investigates serious and organized crime other than:
questions.e: Terror-related crimes are primarily investigated by the NIA, while CBI focuses on other organized crimes and corruption.

questions.q: The CVC Act was passed in which year?
questions.e: Statutory status was conferred on CVC by the Act of 2003.

questions.q: Which Law Commission report dealt with "Prospects of Exempting Income Arising out of Maintenance Money of Minor"?
questions.e: Report No. 265 focused on this specific income exemption issue.

questions.q: The NDMA consists of a chairperson and how many other members?
questions.e: The NDMA has a chairperson and up to nine other members.

questions.q: In most states, the Lokayukta is appointed by:
questions.e: The Governor of the state makes the appointment for Lokayukta and upalokayukta.

questions.q: The CBI functions under the administrative control of:
questions.e: The CBI is under the DoPT of the Ministry of Personnel.

questions.q: The first statutory commission for minorities was constituted in:
questions.e: While the Act was passed in 1992, the Commission was constituted in 1993.

questions.q: Which Law Commission report dealt with "Compulsory Registration of Marriages"?
questions.e: Report No. 270 dealt with the compulsory registration of marriages.

questions.q: The NIA headquarters is located in:
questions.e: The headquarters of the NIA is in New Delhi.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA?
questions.e: The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio chairperson.

questions.q: The Law Commission is a:
questions.e: It is a non-statutory advisory body.

questions.q: The CBI derives its powers from:
questions.e: The CBI derives its powers from the DSPE Act.

questions.q: Which state was first to establish Lokayukta?
questions.e: Maharashtra established it first in 1971.

questions.q: The NDMA works under which Ministry?
questions.e: NDMA is under the administrative control of the Home Ministry.

questions.q: The Bar Council of India was established under which Act?
questions.e: BCI was established under the Advocates Act, 1961.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the first Law Commission of independent India?
questions.e: M.C. Setalvad, the then Attorney-General, was the Chairman of the first Law Commission in 1955.
